semantics.note: The firm 'won't' is a forecast. Reading 'They' as LLMs/transformers and limiting it to Level 5 driving fits the sentence before it. The reliability and outlier remarks are present-tense reasons, and the contract rightly does not score them separately.

contract.note: This is a plain reading of an open-ended negative forecast. A validated Level 5 deployment would contradict it, and only an impossibility result could support it. Separating remote driving from optional advice is an ordinary reading. The contract is fair.

evidence.note: A Waymo company disclosure (Feb 2026) saying it uses advisory remote assistance, not remote drivers. Waymo is not shown to be Level 5 or driven materially by LLMs, so this is context only.
An NVIDIA company disclosure (Aug 2026) about a benchmark ranking. Benchmarks are explicitly not enough, and there is no Level 5 or human-free validation.

reviews.rationale: This forecast has no deadline. The packet shows no independently validated Level 5 system built materially on transformers or LLMs that runs without human help, and no impossibility result. Both items are company disclosures about progress, not proof either way. So the forecast is not yet settled.
